Many and sundry kindes of shewes he set forth: to wit, the Juvenall sports
These youthfull sports Iuvenalia, or Iuvenales ludi, were first instituted by this Nero, privately in houses or gardens, and orchards. Wherein, of all degrees, ages and sexes they daunced and revelled., the Circeian Games, and the Stage-playes: also a Sword fight. In the Juvenall pastimes, he admitted old men even those of Consuls degree: aged women also and matrones to disport themselves. At the Circenses, he appointed places for the Gentlemen of Rome a part by themselves: where hee put also to runne a race for the prise chariots drawne with foure Camels.

In the Stage plaies, (which beeing instituted for the eternizing and perpetuitie of his Empire hee would have to be called Maximi), very many of both degreesGentlemen and Senatours. and sexes plaied their parts upon the Stage. A Romaine Gentleman of very
good note and especiall marke, mounted upon an Elephant ranne downe a ropePer Catadromum, for there were Elephanti Funambuli, vide Galb. cap. 6, et Xiphilinum..
